title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey, September 2026 — the first out-of-sample test of the 6-in-700 mean-reversion base rate, 8:30 a.m. ET on FOMC+1
source: EST: two Philadelphia Fed primaries, both re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) by this event's own never-assessed initial research, independently of the philly-fed-mfg-2026-10-15 sweep that proposed the id. (1) philadelphiafed.org/calendar-of-events?release=manufacturing-business-outlook-survey (131,096 bytes) embeds the full 2026 MBOS schedule as structured data; the September entry reads verbatim {"title":"September Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey","month":"september 2026","day":"17","displayMonth":"Sep","year":"2026","time":"8:30 a.m."}. (2) philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/regional-economic-analysis/manufacturing-business-outlook-survey (277,639 bytes) shows the same release in its next-releases block: 'Sep 17 2026 September Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey 8:30 a.m.' Independently reproduced by the survey's third-Thursday cadence, verified on all twelve 2026 observations rather than inferred: Jan 15 - Feb 19 - Mar 19 - Apr 16 - May 21 - Jun 18 - Jul 16 - Aug 20 - Sep 17 - Oct 15 - Nov 19 - Dec 17, every one at 8:30 a.m. and every one the third Thursday of its month. September 2026's Thursdays are the 3rd, 10th, 17th and 24th, so the third is the 17th. Filed estimate on the two standing counts, neither of which is doubt about the date: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), and this lane does not self-confirm. notes: CANONICAL entry written 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read the one proposal that existed for this id (proposals/philly-fed-mfg-2026-09-17.from-philly-fed-mfg-2026-10-15.json, filed 2026-09-08 by the October Philly lane) and then re-verified both primaries independently. That proposal is now inert and stays where it is. Impact LOW and symbols [] on the grounds the ledger measures rather than assumes: the Third District footprint is sub-state (Delaware, southern New Jersey, eastern and central Pennsylvania), the headline explains R2 ~= 0.20 of national manufacturing IP growth since 2015, and no house playbook is keyed to regional surveys. What earns the row is that this is the DECISION DATE two open ledgers already named as a kill switch, eight days out: philly-fed-mfg-2026-10-15's first kill switch is 'September MBOS (2026-09-17) prints a headline at or above 47.4', and empire-state-mfg-2026-10-15's list names the 09-15/09-17 September pair. Three facts this research adds to the proposal's case. (1) The morning is NOT readable, contrary to the October ledger's own calendar table: 2026-09-17 is FOMC+1 (decision, SEP and dot plot 14:00 ET 2026-09-16), the eve of September triple witching (opex 2026-09-18), and shares 8:30 with weekly jobless claims and housing starts (low, confirmed) - so the identification problem is a macro-digestion one rather than October's co-release one, and it is not smaller. (2) The print's CONTENT is nonetheless pre-FOMC: the Philadelphia Fed's own August 2026 release note states 'Survey results reflect data received through August 17, 2026' against a August 20 release, so September's collection closes around 2026-09-14, two days before the decision. (3) 2026-09-17 is the last day of the FOMC's September blackout (Sep 5-17 per the Philadelphia Fed's own calendar page, an independent Federal Reserve primary corroborating fomc-blackout-start-2026-09-05). This is an ESTIMATE - it widens caution and licenses nothing; the ledger's stance is a permanent stand-aside.
